reference.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: 3D game production reference sheet, intact utility helicopter and its crashed counterpart.
Input image: the factory truck screenshot is STYLE AND SCALE REFERENCE ONLY. Match its hand-painted ochre/olive weathering, readable forms and subdued blue-grey glass. Do not copy screenshot UI.
Create a clean landscape reference sheet on a neutral warm grey background. Four well-separated views: top row intact helicopter side orthographic and front three-quarter; bottom row the SAME helicopter after a crash, side and front three-quarter. A UH-1H Huey-inspired long-cabin utility helicopter: blunt rounded glazed nose, angular framed cockpit windows, broad sliding cabin doors, high single turbine housing, narrow tapered tail boom ending in an upright fin, two-blade main rotor with a compact hub, small two-blade tail rotor and twin tubular skids. Olive drab painted metal, aged cream maintenance marks without text or emblems, rubbed edges, painterly brushwork like the truck. Main rotor diameter about 9.6 game tiles; aircraft nose-to-tail body about 8.6 tiles; cabin roof 2.25 tiles, mast top 3.15 tiles. The reference truck is 4.7 tiles long and 2.36 tiles tall: helicopter body is about 1.8 truck lengths and the helicopter cabin is similar in height to the canvas roof. Include a small side silhouette of that truck at the SAME SCALE along the bottom margin, unobtrusive.
Crashed counterpart keeps the same cabin, nose and paint identity: body slumps left onto a folded skid, one side and belly crumpled, cockpit glass broken away, tail snapped near its root and lying visibly on the ground behind the cabin, main rotor mast broken with both identifiable blades bent and resting on the ground, scattered few attached/deposited pieces of skin. Scorched olive paint and exposed ribs. Show the wreck resting under gravity with broad contact, no floating debris. No fire or smoke hiding the forms, no explosions, no people or injuries, no extra aircraft, no labels, no text. Model-friendly major shapes, rich paint rather than excessive rivet geometry. Each pair must visibly be the same aircraft before and after.

skin.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production texture atlas for a low-poly 3D utility helicopter and crashed version.
The input helicopter sheet is a STYLE AND MATERIAL REFERENCE only. Generate a new texture sheet, not another aircraft illustration.
Create a rectangular texture atlas with exactly FOUR columns and TWO rows, eight equally sized rectangular panels touching edge-to-edge on a perfect regular grid, no gutters, no captions or labels. Every panel is a flat orthographic material painting that fills its cell, edge to edge. Same painterly olive-drab industrial aesthetic and handmade brush strokes as the supplied concept. Broad painted value variation, readable edgewear, irregular scratches and dirt. Keep most detail in these painted materials. Avoid photographic shine, gradients with stripes, excessive tiny noise, labels and rendered objects.
Top row, left to right:
1. OLIVE FUSELAGE: weathered olive green painted aircraft aluminium, warm ochre edge chips, subtle overlapping rectangular access panel seams and sparse rivets. No windows or writing. Medium olive values, not a black field.
2. ENGINE HOUSING: olive metal skin, restrained dark cooling-slot groups near one edge, warm drybrush worn bevels, sparse screws and service-hatch paint. No object silhouette.
3. COCKPIT GLASS: dark desaturated slate blue-grey glazing, broad painted sky reflection strokes, muted warm edge reflection, no window frame or crossbar. Painterly opaque glass.
4. ROTOR AND SKIDS: charcoal grey steel with warm edge rubbing, long subdued brush strokes and sparse chipped beige paint, no lines that divide the panel into a grid.
Bottom row, left to right:
5. SCORCHED OLIVE SKIN: recognizably the same olive paint as panel1 but partly burned, irregular sooty black patches and dark rust, flaking olive/ochre remnants.
6. TORN INNER METAL: dull bare steel and scorched aluminium, uneven brown-black paint, layered jagged edge wear and dark rib-like shadows; flat material image.
7. CABIN FABRIC: old dark olive-brown canvas and leather seat upholstery, broad folds and stitched seams, understated wear.
8. WRECKAGE: very dark warm charcoal, soot, ash, rusty corrugated fragments suggested in paint. Opaque material, not a ground decal.
Subtle tonal depth on every panel, no large blank areas, no transparency, no watermark. Exactly 4 by 2 equal panel layout.

notes: Generated source paintings are retained unchanged. The model uses measured game-truck scale rather than the small truck drawn in the concept sheet.
